text.p: Shares in Swedish telecoms giant Ericsson fell on Thursday morning with brokers partly attributing the dip to U.S. investment bank PaineWebber rating the stock "unattractive".
At 0930 GMT Ericsson was trading five crowns lower at 292 crowns, off a morning low of 290 crowns.
PaineWebber forecast Ericsson would post earnings per share (EPS) of $1.10 for 1997 against consensus of $1.22 and $1.29 in 1998 compared with consensus of $1.54.
"We expect it to lose market share in several segments of its business," PaineWebber said in a report.
PaineWebber said it saw Ericsson losing market share in the overall wireless equipment sector, in the wireline sector and possibly also in its traditionally dominant TDMA business.
"Cellular phones are growing as a percentage of its revenue base, a segment of the market with low margins and one which will see increased competition over the next two years," PaineWebber said.
"It has failed to address several segments of the telecoms market that offer above average growth."
